In this case, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $3x(1+z),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit.

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $3$, and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{x(1+z)}+\frac{1}{3(1+z)} & = \\ \frac{3}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{x(1+z)}+\frac{x}{x}\cdot \frac{1}{3(1+z)} & = \\ \frac{6}{3x(1+z)}+\frac{x}{3x(1+z)} & = \\ \frac{6+x}{3x(1+z)} & \end{aligned}
$$
